A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

α4 integrin is essential for homing to Peyer’s patch, but not for intraepithelial lymphocyte localization, while α5 and αV integrins are not essential for homing of lymphoid cells to any organ, but they may be involved in the inflammatory response.

integrin-mediated adhesion to extracellular matrix proteins is not required for lymphocyte homing to peripheral lymphoid organs, whereas it is essential during leukocyte migration into inflamed tissues and epithelia.
integrin α5, α4, and αV are not essential for the development of T, B, and myeloid cells and that α5, α7, and β7 integrin subunits are not required for homing of T lymphocytes to PPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
integrins play different roles in leukocytes.

the α4β7 integrin is essential for the homing of T lymphocytes to Payer’s patches and for the migration of T lymphocytes in the peritoneal cavity during an inflammatory response, whereas α4β1 is essential for the migration of lymphocytes to the lamina propria and intraepithelial compartment of the gut and to the bone marrow.

the absence of αV or α5 integrins did not produce a significant phenotype in vivo, whereas the absence of the α4 integrins resulted in severe defects in lymphocyte homing to Peyer’s patch, lymphocyte migration into the peritoneal cavity, and lymphocyte development.
